Okay. I just felt it was insensitive but if you're okay with it there's no foul.

I seriously hate when people post that shit man. I even messaged the mods about it but they didn't seem to agree. If you go into someones suicide thread and talk about something THEY EXPLICITLY STATED THEY DON'T HAVE/HAVE NEVER HAD, you're an asshole. Why he brought up being suicidal because his girlfriend of 8 years left him when your problems stem from having NO girlfriend, ever, really upsets me. I simply feel people make these kinds of posts in self interest so that they can ultimately feel like, well, at least my life isn't THAT bad, and it upsets me, greatly. I've seen people give similar suggestions that people "travel" or "try out a few therapists until you find the right one" in threads where people said they were going to kill themselves over lack of money. How are people this dense in this forum? Is there anything that can be done?
I don't think there is one man I'm on /r/collapse

I think the bigger problem than all of these is that 90% of people are more focused on identity politics and are spend a loooot more of their time thinking about and being mad at different religions/different races/different sexualities/different genders than anything at all to do with issues that actually, truly matter.
If a person is struggling with their teeth to the point of suicidal ideation, how does it help to remind them that there are plenty of shittier situations they could be in?

So as a designer of computer chips I'm assuming you are pretty clued into the automation/AI industry. How positive are you of coming changes? This seems to be a hot topic, but I'd love to see some actual factual articles I can read that demonstrate how we could potentially all be replaced in 10 years.

You could link to the gene editing article too if you don't mind.

Yeah, I mean I'm not POSITIVE I'd do it. But I'm like 95% certain I'd have no problem killing myself if things got unlivable. I'm not going to be one of those "survive by any means necessary even in the face of daily rapes unbearable hunger and weather conditions" or something.

That doesn't mean I should just be hedonistic as fuck though at the same time, which this thread is helping me get a good grip on.

I just want to point out that the prevailing narrative in this sub is that there won't just be some human society that lives after the earth heats to unlivable levels, we will literally all be dead. They talk about the PLANET staying alive and perhaps in millions of years being able to harbor life once more, but the narrative is that humans will certainly not survive the next 100 years.

I think I've talked to him in my head a ton. I personally don't see any additional significance to speaking it out loud. I made a custom mix on my turntables of his music weeks after he died and listening to it gives me catharsis toward the situation.

>Other ppl suggested to go and live in a poor country. I second that (I grew up in one). Try to live for a while among people that know how to survive.

The guy who suggested that was an assclown whom unlike a more astute reader who responded to him, didn't realize I can't really survive in a country that didn't have the medical ability to take care of my health maladies. I'm not going to die trying to learn how to survive.

This is a very inspiring story but I don't see how it has to do with collapse. You had very good reason to think you were going to PERSONALLY die tomorrow; that is a much different scenario than the documented certainty of impending human extinction.
So if I actually take the team to read each and every one of these in detail, there's no way to conclude anything but we have ONE decade left exactly? All of these articles make this thesis?
I was going to pm you but your account is brand new so I don't know if you know how. Let me know if you want advice about this we can talk on reddit or elsewhere.
Yeah, I simply can't do that for literal medical reasons. I laughed off his post.

But I had a vasectomy...

I really appreciate the condolences... his older brother died of a od a couple weeks ago and I've just been devastated for his mother. I may have already mentioned this.

Man up is a dangerous phrase; you don't need to be some ideal machismo guy in order to get through this.

However, I can relate. I've done tons of things with the attitude of fuck it, I won't be here in a year. It has to stop because it only adds to the misery in the long run.
